# Generation 6 — Gevurah Release Risk Map

The Awtsmoos gives expanding light a vessel whose border keeps truth whole;
Awtsmoos.com must not trade a fast release for a broken corpus, stale branch, or uncontrolled role.

## Critical risks

1. Replaying an already-accepted corpus mirror and corrupting custody.
2. Treating intentionally ignored runtime data as Git-owned source.
3. Letting the clean worktree miss runtime corpus needed by real integrity tests.
4. Staging ignored corpus files or unrelated concurrent-agent files.
5. Overwriting newer upstream `HtmlCompactModules.js` or other remote-owned changes.
6. Trusting source-checkout tests instead of clean latest-origin integration tests.
7. Pushing after origin/main moves.
8. Deploying a SHA not equal to pushed remote main.
9. Confusing local server success with production activation.
10. Confusing cached search/crawler views with current origin behavior.
11. Weakening crawl verification to make a release pass.
12. Fabricating SEO metadata absent from source data.
13. Adding speculative features after the release candidate is already proven, increasing blast radius.
14. Declaring completion before public raw HTTPS and browser-shadow evidence exist.
15. Leaving durable REMAINING_WORK stale after success or failure.

## Restraint law

Finish the current candidate first. Any new architecture discovered now must enter future-evolution memory unless it closes a concrete defect observed by tests, runtime, integration, or production.
